transcript.text: Sometimes when I open the dishwasher there's grey smelly water in the bottom even though it finished draining fine. Not every day though. Kitchen sink was replaced last month if that matters.

That intermittent grey water is often caused by food debris sitting at the bottom of the tub or a partial blockage in the drain path, which can be linked to your recent sink work. Since the machine drains fine most times, it’s likely just a bit of gunk getting stuck rather than a failed pump. To check this safely, please switch off and unplug the dishwasher first, then remove the lower rack and twist out the filter at the bottom. Rinse the filter under the tap and look into the sump hole with a torch to see if there is any food or glass trapped underneath.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
Ok, I've taken the filter out and it's clean, nothing stuck in the sump either. It seems to happen after I drain the sink full of washing-up water, if that helps. The sink drains a little slow too.

Since the filter and sump are clear, this points to a blockage further down in the drain hose or at the sink waste connection itself. The fact that your sink drains slowly suggests there is likely debris trapped where the dishwasher hose joins the sink plumbing. Please check the grey drain hose along its length for kinks, and look under the sink at the joint with the waste pipe to ensure it is tight and not blocked by a loose plug or food. To help me find the correct replacement parts if needed, could you please provide the make and model number of your dishwasher? This is usually found on a label on the side edge of the door frame.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's a Hotpoint HFC 3C26 W. I looked under the sink: since the new sink went in, the drain hose just lies on the cupboard floor and goes straight into the waste spigot, with no high loop in it.

That missing high loop is almost certainly why you are getting grey water back into the dishwasher. Without it, any time you run the sink and it drains slowly, the dirty sink water flows straight back down the hose into your machine because there is no air gap to stop it. To fix this safely, please switch off and unplug the appliance first, then lift the drain hose so it forms a high loop under the worktop before dropping down to the waste spigot. This creates an air break that stops sink water from siphoning back into the dishwasher when you wash up.
